title: What Is the Placebo Effect, Really?
summary: Explore what a placebo is, how expectations and psychological mechanisms can relieve pain and symptoms, and why the effect remains debated.
evidenceNote: While placebo responses for subjective outcomes like pain are well-documented, overall clinical relevance and the exact size of the effect remain widely debated among researchers.

scenes.text: Can a sugar pill make your pain actually go away?
A placebo is a medicine or treatment intended to appear genuine, but with no pharmaceutical effect.
Modern studies find placebos can affect subjective outcomes like pain and nausea, but do not impact the disease itself.
Placebos relieve symptoms through psychological mechanisms, yet they remain widely misunderstood.
